rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exalting God from what is unfit prepares for knowledge of His perfection; this passage names that prerequisite because it describes qualities leading believers to His light.
rows.anchor: والآية في مقام بيان خصالهم التي تستدعي هدايتهم إلى نوره فلا جرم اقتصر فيها بذكر ما هي المقدمة وهو التسبيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Commerce denotes sustained earning through buying and selling, while a sale is a discrete transaction; together the negations cover continuous and occasional distraction from God.
rows.anchor: التجارة إذا قوبلت بالبيع كان المفهوم منها بحسب العرف الاستمرار في الاكتساب بالبيع والشراء والبيع هو العمل الاكتسابي الدفعي

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative says profitable sales are negated separately because their immediate gain can distract even when the trade as a profession does not.
rows.anchor: وقيل الوجه في نفي البيع بعد نفي إلهاء التجارة أن الربح في البيع ناجز بالفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i calls the explanation for separately negating sale a good one; repeating the negative particle reinforces the denial.
rows.anchor: لتذكير النفي وتأكيده، وهو وجه حسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form iqām is a shortened form of iqāma, with the tāʾ omitted for ease of pronunciation.
rows.anchor: الإقام هو الإقامة بحذف التاء تخفيفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Establishing prayer and giving zakat represent all commanded good works; prayer stands for duties toward God and zakat for duties toward creation, each being a central pillar.
rows.anchor: والمراد بإقامة الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة الإتيان بجميع الأعمال الصالحة التي كلف الله تعالى عباده بإتيانها في حياتهم الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because prayer and zakat are also remembrance, their contrast with remembrance points to inward, knowing remembrance of God, opposite forgetfulness and heedlessness.
rows.anchor: والمقابلة بين ذكر الله وبين إقام الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة وهما - وخاصة الصلاة - من ذكر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse pairs sustained commerce and individual sales with constant inward remembrance and time-bound acts of worship: neither kind of distraction diverts them.
rows.anchor: لا يشتغلون بشيء عن ذكرهم المستمر بقلوبهم لربهم وذكرهم الموقت بأعمالهم من الصلاة والزكاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feared day is Resurrection, and the definite plural hearts and eyes includes those of both believers and disbelievers.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالقلوب والأبصار ما يعم قلوب المؤمنين والكافرين وأبصارهم لكون القلوب والأبصار جمعا محلى باللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At Resurrection, worldly perception that distracts from God and veils truth gives way to perception through faith and knowledge; believers see God's generosity, while disbelievers are blind and meet what pains them.
rows.anchor: فتنصرف القلوب والأبصار يومئذ عن المشاهدة والرؤية الدنيوية الشاغلة عن الله الساترة للحق والحقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This description is singled out because the passage concerns the means by which God guides people to the faith and knowledge that will illuminate their sight in the next life.
rows.anchor: أن الكلام مسوق لبيان ما يتوسل به إلى هدايته تعالى إلى نوره وهو نور الإيمان والمعرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He interprets hearts and eyes here as souls and their inner insights.
rows.anchor: أن المراد بالقلوب والأبصار النفوس وبصائرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The turning of perception explains their fear: one outcome is permanent deprivation of God's light and honor, ending in lasting misery and punishment; ultimately they fear themselves.
rows.anchor: يخافون هذا التقلب لما في أحد شقيه من الحرمان من نور الله والنظر إلى كرامته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose clause means God rewards them with the best act in each category; He refines their deeds by overlooking defects and counting the good as best.
rows.anchor: معناه أنه يجزيهم بإزاء عملهم في كل باب جزاء أحسن عمل في ذلك الباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing promise that God provides without account supports a generous, uncritical reckoning of good deeds.
rows.anchor: ظاهرة عدم المداقة في حساب الحسنات بالإغماض عن جهات نقصها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise of whatever the pious wish, together with a further gift, shows that God's increase exceeds human desire and effort.
rows.anchor: حيث إن ظاهره أن هذا المزيد الموعود أمر وراء ما تتعلق به مشيئتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran promises the pious whatever they wish as recompense, so the further increase must be something greater than their wishes.
rows.anchor: هذا المزيد الذي هو وراء جزاء الأعمال أمر أعلى وأعظم من أن تتعلق به مشية الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bounty clause resumes the explanation that God guides whom He wills; He grants both the best recompense for deeds and a further gift by His will.
rows.anchor: استئناف مآله تعليل الجملتين السابقتين بالمشية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised recompense corresponds to deeds, as the verse about each soul receiving what it earned states, but the extra bounty is not earned or owed.
rows.anchor: وما في معناه من الآيات لكنه تعالى يجزيهم بكل عمل من أعمالهم جزاء أحسن عمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has pledged the basic reward and sworn that it is true; He has not made the surplus an entitlement, so its allocation rests on His will.
rows.anchor: فملكهم الاستحقاق لأصله وهو الذي يجزيهم به على قدر أعمالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mirage is a desert shimmer with no substance; qīʿa and qāʿ mean level ground, and their singular forms follow patterns like tīn and tamr.
rows.anchor: والقيع والقاع هو المستوي من الأرض ومفرداهما القيعة والقاعة كالتينة والتمرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers' offerings, invocations, and other devotional acts toward idols promise an outcome but have no reality to reach.
rows.anchor: أعمالهم تارة بأنها لا حقيقة لها كسراب بقيعة فلا غاية لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only someone driven by thirst travels toward apparent water, explaining why the simile specifies the thirsty person and says he eventually finds nothing.
rows.anchor: لأن المطلوب بيان سيره إليه ولا يسير إليه إلا الظمآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers' empty actions contrast with believers who remember God in the houses He honored and are not distracted by trade or sale.
rows.anchor: ووصفهم بأنهم ذاكرون له في بيوت معظمة لا تلهيهم عنه تجارة ولا بيع،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying the thirsty person 'came to it' hints that someone is waiting for him; the following words identify God as the one who meets him.
rows.anchor: هناك من يريد مجيئه وينتظره انتظارا وهو الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fulfilling the account is a figure for giving a person the recompense warranted by the calculation of his deeds.
rows.anchor: وتوفية الحساب كناية عن الجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their deeds are a mirage and they are thirsty pursuers who ignore a master offering real water; at death they find no reward from their acts or idols.
rows.anchor: وتشبيههم بالظمآن الذي يريد الماء وعنده عذب الماء لكنه يعرض عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's reckoning is swift because His knowledge encompasses small and great matters, subtle and obvious, earlier and later alike.
rows.anchor: لاحاطة علمه بالقليل والكثير والحقير والخطير والدقيق والجليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The point also applies to deniers of the Creator: everyone seeks happiness, but those who rely on nature, matter, or time discover worldly striving has no lasting result at death.
rows.anchor: فإن الإنسان كائنا من كان يرى لنفسه سعادة في الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second simile presents their deeds as layered barriers that keep their hearts from the light of knowledge, like darknesses in a deep sea.
rows.anchor: تشبيه ثان لأعمالهم يظهر به أنها حجب متراكمة على قلوبهم تحجبهم عن نور المعرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A deep sea is one whose waves churn; waves, further waves, and clouds block sunlight, moonlight, and starlight, while repeated darkness means layers piled atop one another.
rows.anchor: يحجبنه جميعا من الاستضاءة بأضواء الشمس والقمر والنجوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If a person can barely see the hand placed closest before the eyes, the darkness is at its extreme; the image gives the travelers no light toward salvation.
rows.anchor: فإذا أخرج يده ولم يكد يراها كانت الظلمة بالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one besides God creates light, so one to whom God has given no light has none.
rows.anchor: فإذا لم يجعل لشيء نورا لم يكن له نورا إذ لا جاعل غيره تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After contrasting believers' light and disbelievers' lack of it, the following verses argue for God's light through universal glorification and the signs of creation.
rows.anchor: شرع يحتج على ذلك بما في هذه الآية والآيات الأربع التالية لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything in the heavens and earth exists through God, since nothing within them can be the self-sufficient source of another needy thing's existence.
rows.anchor: فوجود ما فيهما من موجود من الله الذي ينتهي إليه الحاجات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each thing's existence is bestowed by God and reveals Him as its source; because God makes everything manifest, all creation glorifies Him by showing its dependence and lack of any independent lord.
rows.anchor: ولازمه نفي الاستقلال عن كل من سواه وسلب أي إله ورب يدبر الأمر دونه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse highlights rational beings and birds in flight despite universal glorification because conscious creatures and birds' formation are especially wondrous signs of creation.
rows.anchor: ولعل ذلك من باب اختيار أمور من أعاجيب الخلقة للذكر

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some take those in the heavens and earth to mean all things, using rational language because their glorification resembles rational speech or their sign is exceptionally clear.
rows.anchor: وإنما عبر بلفظ أولي العقل لكون التسبيح المنسوب إليها من شؤون أولي العقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects that broad reading because the next clause explicitly says every one of them knows its prayer and glorification.
rows.anchor: وفيه أنه لا يلائم إسناد العلم إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that God is the Light of the heavens and earth is supported by the way all existence points beyond itself to its source.
rows.anchor: لأن النور هو ما يظهر به الشيء المستنير ثم يدل بظهوره على مظهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening 'Have you not seen' signals a manifest sign; the address is general to every rational person, though it could specifically address the Prophet, whom God showed the kingdom of creation.
rows.anchor: ومن الممكن أن يكون خطابا خاصا بالنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وقد كان أراه الله تسبيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet may have witnessed creation glorifying God, as people reportedly saw a pebble glorify God in his hand; the cited reports are deemed reliable.
rows.anchor: وقد أرى الناس تسبيح الحصاة في كفه كما وردت به الأخبار المعتبرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse attributes knowledge of prayer and glorification to all the beings it names; discussion of universal glorification is linked to earlier and later Quran commentary.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم بعض البحث عنه في تفسير قوله وإن من شيء إلا يسبح بحمده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects reading the subject of 'knows' as God because that does not fit the syntax and especially the following statement that God knows what they do.
rows.anchor: يدفعه عدم ملائمته للسياق وخاصة

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Others treat attributing knowledge to all creatures as figurative, comparing non-rational beings to knowers because their signs clearly show glorification.
rows.anchor: إن إسناد العلم إلى مجموع ما تقدم من المجاز بتنزيل غير العالم منزلة العالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage stresses glorification rather than praise because its argument against associating partners with God is most directly made by denying that others share His divine uniqueness.
rows.anchor: فإن من يدعو من دون الله إلها آخر أو يركن إلى غيره نوعا من الركون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is supplication for a need; since the one addressed is free of the supplicant's need, prayer itself points especially to God's transcendence.
rows.anchor: فصلاته دعاؤه والدعاء توجيه من الداعي للمدعو إلى حاجته ففيه دلالة على حاجة عند الداعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All creatures, believers and disbelievers alike, share a universal light, while God's special light is reserved for His believing friends.
rows.anchor: أن هناك نورين نور عام يعم الأشياء والمؤمن والكافر فيه سواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Universal knowledge and glorification recall primordial testimony and the unveiling of sight, while the special light belongs to believers; divine light, like mercy, is general and particular.
rows.anchor: فالنور الذي ينور تعالى به خلقه كالرحمة التي يرحمهم بها قسمان عام وخاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling glorification their deed is valid even when at some levels it is identical with their existence; divine knowledge of it encourages believers and completes the proof against deniers whose acts are recorded.
rows.anchor: وهذا التسبيح وإن كان في بعض المراحل هو نفس وجودهم لكن صدق اسم التسبيح يجوز أن يعد فعلا لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's ownership and the return to Him mediate between the proof of universal light and the proof of special light, establishing His unrestricted authority over all things.
rows.anchor: يعطي أنها كالمتوسط بين القبيلين أعني بين الأمرين يحتج بها على كليهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God alone owns everything, He may act and judge as He wills; the return here means all affairs revert to Him, not specifically the afterlife.
rows.anchor: مرجعيته تعالى في الأمور دون المعاد نظير قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Izjāʾ means to drive, rukām means piled up, wadq is rain, and khilāl are gaps; the address to the Prophet as hearer extends to every observer.
rows.anchor: والخلال جمع الخلل وهو الفرجة بين الشيئين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God drives separate clouds by winds, joins and piles them up, and rain emerges through their gaps.
rows.anchor: يدفع بالرياح سحابا متفرقا ثم يؤلف بينه ثم يجعله متراكما بعضه على بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The upper sky is the direction above; mountains of hail describes its abundance and accumulation, and sanāʾ means light.
rows.anchor: والبرد قطعات الجمد النازل من السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sends accumulated hail that can ruin fields and gardens and sometimes kill people or livestock, while sparing whom He wills; lightning nearly blinds the eyes.
rows.anchor: فيفسد المزارع والبساتين وربما قتل النفوس والمواشي ويصرفه عمن يشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The weather signs explain why God's special light belongs to whom He wills: He may send beneficial rain or damaging hail, choosing who is struck and spared.
rows.anchor: مسوقة لتعليل ما تقدم من اختصاصه المؤمنين بنوره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following alternation of night and day further demonstrates that events are governed solely by God's will.
rows.anchor: بيان آخر الرجوع الأمر إلى مشيته تعالى فقط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report applies the lamp parable to the believer: his heart's light nearly shines even before he speaks, and obligations and sunna illuminate one another.
rows.anchor: يكاد النور الذي في قلبه يضيء وإن لم يتكلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report lists five lights for the believer: entry, departure, knowledge, speech, and final arrival in paradise.
rows.anchor: فالمؤمن يتقلب في خمسة من النور مدخله نور، ومخرجه نور، وعلمه نور، وكلامه نور

rows.speaker: جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Asked whether the parable is of God's own light, Ja'far denies that God has a likeness; al-Tabataba'i says the likeness concerns light bestowed by God, avoiding incarnation or transformation.
rows.anchor: قلت لجعفر عليه السلام إنهم يقولون مثل نور الرب. قال سبحان الله ليس لله مثل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in 'His likeness' may refer to God if the verse is understood as a likeness of His light bestowed on creation, not of the divine essence.
rows.anchor: فكونه مثلا له تعالى يؤدي إلى الحلول أو الانقلاب تعالى عن ذلك

rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report in al-Tawhid says the niche parable is for the Prophet and Imams, who guide to divine unity, religious interests, Islamic law, and obligations and sunna.
rows.anchor: فقال هو مثل ضربه الله لنا فالنبي والأئمة صلوات الله عليهم من دلالات الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet and his purified household are among the finest applications of the verse; its apparent scope includes other prophets, successors, and saints, but not every believer because its described qualities are not universal.
rows.anchor: فالآية تعم بظاهرها غيرهم من الأنبياء عليهم السلام والأوصياء والأولياء

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Kafi's report through Jabir applies the niche to Muhammad's heart, its lamp to the knowledge within him, the glass to Ali or his heart, and the blessed tree to Abraham, who was neither Jew nor Christian.
rows.anchor: بإسناده عن جابر عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام وفيها أن المشكاة قلب محمد صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: In that application, the near-shining oil represents Muhammad's descendants nearly speaking prophecy even without an angel descending to them.
rows.anchor: يكاد أولادهم أن يتكلموا بالنبوة وإن لم ينزل عليهم ملك

rows.speaker: الباقر عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report in al-Tawhid identifies the niche as knowledge in the Prophet's chest and the glass as Ali's chest; a scholar of Muhammad's family nearly speaks knowledge before being asked, and each Imam follows the prior one with knowledge and wisdom.
rows.anchor: إلى عيسى بن راشد عن الباقر عليه السلام وفيه أن المشكاة نور العلم في صدر النبي

rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: An al-Kafi application identifies the niche with Fatima, the lamp with Hasan, the glass with Husayn, Abraham as the tree, and the Imams as light upon light.
rows.anchor: عن صالح بن سهل الهمداني عن الصادق عليه السلام وفيه أن المشكاة فاطمة عليها السلام

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Ibn Mardawayh transmits from the Prophet that the olive tree neither eastern nor western means Abraham's heart was neither Jewish nor Christian; al-Tabataba'i calls this an illustrative application.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم في قوله { زيتونة لا شرقية ولا غربية } قال

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك وبريدة
rows.claim: A report says the houses God commanded to be raised are the houses of prophets; the Prophet calls Ali and Fatima's house one of the best. Al-Tabataba'i treats it as an application, also transmitted mursal in al-Majma and through Jabir from Abu Ja'far in al-Qummi.
rows.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك وبريدة قالا

rows.speaker: علي عليه السلام
rows.claim: In a Nahj al-Balagha sermon, Ali describes people of remembrance who trade the world for remembrance, warn the heedless, enjoin justice, and forbid wrong.
rows.anchor: وفي نهج البلاغة من كلام له عليه السلام عند تلاوته

rows.speaker: علي عليه السلام
rows.claim: Ali portrays them as living in this world as if already in the next, aware of barzakh and resurrection and revealing what ordinary people cannot see or hear.
rows.anchor: كأنما قطعوا الدنيا إلى الآخرة وهم فيها فشاهدوا ما وراء ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Different applications of the parable in Shia reports show that they are examples, not exclusive interpretations of its words.
rows.anchor: أقول وهو من قبيل ذكر بعض المصاديق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The constellations and meteors in the visible sky that repel devils correspond to guidance through prophethood, which lights the human world; this contextual interpretation does not cancel the verse's plain sense.
rows.anchor: وأشار بذلك إلى ما يناظره في الحقيقة من إضاءة العالم الإنساني بنور الهداية من الرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khilfa means something that replaces another; night and day succeed one another and each can serve for remembrance or gratitude when the other has passed.
rows.anchor: الخلفة هي الشيء يسد مسد شيء آخر وبالعكس وكأنه بناء نوع أريد به معنى الوصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembrance means returning to innate proofs of God's unity and attributes, culminating in faith; gratitude is speech or action praising His gifts, including worship and good works.
rows.anchor: المراد بالتذكر الرجوع إلى ما يعرفه الإنسان بفطرته من الحجج الدالة على توحيد ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternating night and day is a favor: one may recover faith, worship, or a good deed missed during one period in the other.
rows.anchor: فمن فاته الإيمان به في هذه البرهة من الزمان تداركه في البرهة الأخرى منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse links back to the sun and moon: though the arrogant are kept from ascending to God's presence, servants can still approach and receive guidance by alternating daylight and moonlit night.
rows.anchor: فجعل نهارا ذا شمس طالعة وليلا ذا قمر منير وهما ذوا خلفة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some interpret remembrance as the obligatory prayer and gratitude as the voluntary prayer; al-Tabataba'i says the verse can fit this reading but does not require it.
rows.anchor: وفسر بعضهم التذكر بصلاة الفريضة والشكور بالنافلة والآية تقبل الانطباق على ذلك

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: The quoted Prophetic report, introduced just before this segment as transmitted from Abu Umama, says the greatest deity worshipped under heaven besides God is a desire that is followed.
rows.anchor: ما تحت ظل السماء من إله يعبد من دون الله أعظم عند الله من هوى متبع

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Qummi transmits from Abu al-Jarud that the shadow in this verse is the interval from dawn until sunrise.
rows.anchor: في تفسير القمي في رواية أبي الجارود عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام

rows.speaker: ابن سيرين
rows.claim: Ibn Sirin says the verse about creation from water was revealed concerning Muhammad and Ali: Ali is both the Prophet's cousin and son-in-law, joining blood kinship and marriage.
rows.anchor: قال ابن سيرين نزلت في النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وعلي بن أبي طالب زوج فاطمة عليا فهو ابن عمه وزوج ابنته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the disbeliever who supported others against his Lord as Abu al-Hakam, whom the Prophet named Abu Jahl; al-Tabataba'i says these two preceding reports resemble illustrative applications.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن جرير وابن مردويه عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Qummi's report lists the visible stars and the twelve zodiac signs, with four assigned to each of spring, summer, autumn, and winter.
rows.anchor: فالبروج الكواكب والبروج التي للربيع والصيف الحمل والثور

rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Faqih transmits al-Sadiq's instruction to make up what was missed at night during the day and what was missed by day at night, citing the alternating night and day.
rows.anchor: وفي الفقيه قال الصادق عليه السلام كلما فاتك بالليل فاقضه بالنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the third proof from God's acts, chiefly aimed at establishing resurrection; since denial of resurrection undermines law and religion, the Prophet is directed toward those ready to believe.
rows.anchor: بيان هذا هو الفصل الثالث من الآيات المحتجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wind stirs and spreads clouds, God stretches them in the upper air as He wills and divides them into masses, and rain falls through their gaps to give life to people, animals, and plants.
rows.anchor: فتحرك وتنشر سحابا ويبسط ذلك السحاب في جهة العلو من الجو كيف يشاء سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ethāra is stirring and spreading, sky is whatever is above and shelters, kasaf is plural for pieces, wadq is rain, and khilāl are openings.
rows.anchor: الإثارة التحريك والنشر والسحاب الغمام والسماء جهة العلو فكل ما علاك وأظلك فهو سماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblās means despair; if both pronouns refer to rain, the repeated 'before it' emphasizes how quickly people move from despair to joy.
rows.anchor: وفائدة التأكيد - على ما قيل - الإعلام بسرعة تقلب قلوب البشر من اليأس إلى الاستبشار

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf reads the repetition as emphasizing that rain had long been withheld, so despair deepened and their joy matched their prior grief.
rows.anchor: وفي الكشاف أن قوله { من قبله } من باب التكرير والتوكيد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reading makes the pronoun refer to the sending of winds: they were hopeless before rain and before the winds were sent.
rows.anchor: وربما قيل أن ضمير { من قبله } لإرسال الرياح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's mercy here is rain; its traces are plants, trees, and fruits, which in turn are the traces of the earth's restored life and of divine planning.
rows.anchor: وآثارها ما يترتب على نزول المطر من النبات والأشجار والأثمار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The initial weakness is the starting point of human creation, especially early childhood though it may also include the embryo; strength is maturity, and later weakness is old age, with gray hair clarifying it.
rows.anchor: ومصداقه على ما تفيده المقابلة أول الطفولية وإن أمكن صدقه على النطفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite words weakness and strength leave their degree unspecified because people differ in their measure.
rows.anchor: للدلالة على الإبهام وعدم تعين المقدار لاختلاف الأفراد في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The successive stages are each acts of creation, not a separate human deity's governance; God is therefore the Creator, All-Knowing and Powerful.
rows.anchor: وفي ذلك أتم الإشارة إلى أن تتالي هذه الأحوال من الخلق وإذ كان هذا النقل من حال إلى حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The criminals' short estimate of their stay follows their lifelong distortion of truth: they misread the interval between death and resurrection as only an hour of worldly time.
rows.anchor: فيظنون أنهم لم يلبثوا في قبورهم فيما بين الموت والبعث غير ساعة من نهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They judge the resurrection by the world's order because they are absorbed in earthly life and know little beyond it; thus the truth appears false to them, with no excuse.
rows.anchor: لإخلادهم إلى الأرض وتوغلهم في نشأة الدنيا يرون يوم البعث والفصل بينه وبين الدنيا محكوما بنظام الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'They were turned away' means they persistently turn from truth to falsehood, treating clear proofs as fables when called to the truth.
rows.anchor: فيدعون إلى الحق ويقام عليه الحجج والآيات فيظنونه باطلا من القول وخرافة من الرأي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those given knowledge and faith answer that the criminals remained according to God's Book until Resurrection; the criminals had treated the afterlife as a brief worldly interval.
rows.anchor: فإن المجرمين لإخلادهم إلى الأرض

rows.speaker: مجمع البيان
rows.claim: Al-Majma explains iṣṭirākh as crying out and calling for help, derived from ṣarākh.
rows.anchor: في المجمع الاصطراخ الصياح والنداء بالاستغاثة افتعال من الصراخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request to be brought out explains the cries; God's question about granting a life in which one could remember answers them, and the commands to taste punishment and the denial of any helper follow from that answer.
rows.anchor: بيان لاصطراخهم، وقوله { أولم نعمركم ما يتذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of the Fire ask to return and do good unlike their former deeds, but are told that they had time and a warner, failed to believe, and have no rescuer from punishment.
rows.anchor: فذوقوا العذاب فما للظالمين من نصير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God judges people by their inner beliefs and the effects of their deeds, whether their outward appearance agrees with their inward state or not.
rows.anchor: فيعاملكم بما في باطنكم من الاعتقاد وآثار الأعمال ويحاسبكم عليه سواء وافق ظاهركم باطنكم أو خالف

rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Majma reports al-Sadiq's definition of scholars as those whose actions match their words; someone whose deeds contradict their speech is not a scholar, and the most knowledgeable of God are most fearful of Him.
rows.anchor: روي عن الصادق عليه السلام أنه قال يعني بالعلماء من صدق قوله فعله

rows.speaker: أبو حمزة عن علي بن الحسين عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report in Rawdat al-Kafi from Abu Hamza, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, conveys the same point about true knowledge and fear of God.
rows.anchor: وفي روضة الكافي بإسناده عن أبي حمزة عن علي بن الحسين عليه السلام ما في معناه

rows.speaker: الحسن عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: A report transmitted by Ibn Abi Shayba, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Hakim distinguishes useful knowledge in the heart from knowledge on the tongue, which is God's proof against people.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reports the Prophet interpreting God's increase from bounty as intercession for someone liable to Hell who had done him a kindness in worldly life.
rows.anchor: وفي المجمع روى ابن مسعود عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: الرضا عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Kafi reports al-Rida saying the chosen inheritors are Fatima's descendants: the forerunner is the Imam, the moderate knows the Imam, and the wrongdoer does not know him.
rows.anchor: عن أحمد بن عمر قال سألت أبا الحسن الرضا عليه السلام

rows.speaker: الباقر عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report from Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i says the verse specifically concerns the Prophet's family: the forerunners are Ali, Hasan, Husayn, and a martyr among them; the moderate fasts by day and worships at night; the wrongdoer among people is forgiven.
rows.anchor: لأبي إسحاق السبيعي عن الباقر عليه السلام في الآية قال هي لنا خاصة يا أبا إسحاق

rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq describes the wrongdoer as revolving around the self, the moderate around the heart, and the forerunner around the Lord.
rows.anchor: وفي معاني الأخبار مسندا عن الصادق عليه السلام في الآية قال الظالم يحوم حوم نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i explains self-orbiting as following desire, heart-orbiting as purifying the heart through ascetic worship, and Lord-orbiting as exclusive devotion, hope, and intention toward God.
rows.anchor: ودوران الظالم لنفسه حوم نفسه اتباعه أهواءها وسعيه في تحصيل ما يرضيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many Shia reports from the Ahl al-Bayt restrict the verse's application to Fatima's descendants.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن الروايات من طرق الشيعة عن أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام في كون الآية خاصة بولد فاطمة عليها السلام كثيرة جدا

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: A report collected in al-Durr al-Manthur says forerunners enter Paradise without reckoning, moderates face an easy reckoning, and wrongdoers are held for a long gathering before receiving God's mercy.
rows.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم يقول

rows.speaker: عمر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet by Umar calls the wrongdoer in the inheritors verse a disbeliever; al-Tabataba'i says this contradicting report is not given weight.
rows.anchor: عن عمر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qummi glosses naṣab as toil and laghūb as fatigue and vexation.
rows.anchor: قال النصب العناء واللغوب الكسل والضجر

rows.speaker: علي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A saying in Nahj al-Balagha sets the age by which God has given a person sufficient excuse at sixty years; al-Majma and al-Durr also transmit it from Ali.
rows.anchor: وقال العمر الذي أعذر الله فيه إلى ابن آدم ستون سنة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: A report says that on Judgment Day it will be asked where the sixty-year-olds are, identifying them as those given the life mentioned in the verse; other routes cite Sahl ibn Sa'd and Abu Hurayra.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: الباقر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Another reported interpretation makes the rebuke apply to someone who reached eighteen years; it is attributed to al-Baqir and transmitted in al-Faqih.
rows.anchor: وفي المجمع وقيل هو توبيخ لابن ثماني عشر سنة وروي ذلك عن الباقر عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing section argues for God's sole lordship from human succession on earth and His sustaining the heavens and earth, denies lordship to idols, rebukes broken oaths and plotting, and warns that God delays but does not fail to punish.
rows.anchor: بيان احتجاج على توحيد الربوبية كقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each human generation succeeds its predecessor and gains comparable use of the earth; this succession is bound to procreation and creation, so it is a form of governance inseparable from creation.
rows.anchor: وكون الناس خلائف في الأرض هو قيام كل لاحق منهم مقام سابقه وسلطته على التصرف والانتفاع منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God creates humanity and makes generations successors, He alone governs them; even opponents concede that God is the Creator, so He is their Lord.
rows.anchor: فخالق الإنسان هو رب الإنسان لكن الخالق هو الله سبحانه حتى عند الخصم فالله هو رب الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelief harms the disbeliever by bringing divine contempt and personal loss, replacing human happiness with misery in the journey to the next life.
rows.anchor: أن كفرهم يورث لهم مقتا عند ربهم والمقت شدة البغض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text says contempt is 'with their Lord' because it comes from God, while loss is the person's own consequence of changing faith and happiness into disbelief and misery.
rows.anchor: لأن الخسار من تبعات تبديل الإيمان كفرا والسعادة شقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording 'increase' reflects human nature as open to development: faith increases perfection and nearness to God, while disbelief increases contempt and loss.
rows.anchor: لأن الفطرة الإنسانية بسيطة ساذجة واقعة في معرض الاستكمال والازدياد فإن أسلم الإنسان زاده ذلك كمالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine love and hatred are attributes of action, not intrinsic qualities: love is mercy extending toward someone and hatred is its withdrawal.
rows.anchor: والحب والبغض المنسوبان إلى الله سبحانه من صفات الأفعال وهي معان خارجة عن الذات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge to name the partners shows that God alone can create and sustain; the section threatens those who break their sworn claims and plot evil.
rows.anchor: وتوبيخ وتهديد لهم على نقضهم ما أبرموه باليمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not punish them immediately but postpones judgment to an appointed term, death or resurrection; when it arrives, He repays their deeds because He sees His servants.
rows.anchor: فلا يؤاخذهم ولكن يؤخرهم إلى أجل مسمى وهو الموت أو البعث فإذا جاء أجلهم عاملهم بما عملوا

rows.speaker: مجمع البيان
rows.claim: Al-Majma defines ṭams as erasing something until no trace remains, including removing the eye's cleft so sight is lost.
rows.anchor: قال في مجمع البيان الطمس محو الشيء حتى يذهب أثره فالطمس على العين كالطمس على الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God willed, He could erase their eyes completely and end their ability to see; racing toward the clear path would not let them see it, and the question implies this is impossible for them.
rows.anchor: أي لو أردنا لأذهبنا أعينهم فصارت ممسوحة لا أثر منها فذهبت به أبصارهم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some interpret racing toward the path as trying to follow the way of truth without finding guidance.
rows.anchor: وقول بعضهم إن المراد باستباق الصراط مبادرتهم إلى سلوك طريق الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i says that alternative interpretation is somewhat far-fetched.
rows.anchor: لا يخلو من بعد

rows.speaker: مجمع البيان
rows.claim: Al-Majma defines transformation as changing a person's form into a distorted creature and says makāna means place.
rows.anchor: قال في المجمع والمسخ قلب الصورة إلى خلقة مشوهة كما مسخ قوم قردة وخنازير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being transformed in place means God could deform them where they sit without moving them or using any process; the ease of this is expressed figuratively.
rows.anchor: والمراد بمسخهم على مكانتهم تشويه خلقهم وهم قعود في مكانهم الذي هم فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their inability to proceed or return means they cannot move into punishment or regain their former safe state; the alternative reading about going to destinations and homes is unlikely.
rows.anchor: فالمضي والرجوع كنايتان عن الرجوع إلى حال السلامة والبقاء على حال العذاب والمسخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A long life reverses human development: strength weakens, increase diminishes, knowledge becomes ignorance, and memory becomes forgetfulness; this demonstrates God's power to blind or transform them.
rows.anchor: والإنسان في عهد الهرم منكس الخلق يتبدل قوته ضعفا وعلمه جهلا وذكره نسيانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing question rebukes the audience for failing to reason and urges them to reflect on these signs.
rows.anchor: توبيخهم على عدم التعقل وحثهم على التدبر في هذه الأمور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denial that Muhammad was taught poetry returns to the surah's opening affirmation that he is a messenger and his book is revealed remembrance, not poetry.
rows.anchor: عطف ورجوع إلى ما تقدم في صدر السورة من تصديق رسالة النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو بكر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: Reports describe the Prophet quoting a poetic line about the days revealing what one did not know; Abu Bakr corrected his wording, and the Prophet said he was not a poet and should not be one.
rows.anchor: فجعل يقول ويأتيك من لم تزود بالأخبار فيقول أبو بكر ليس هكذا يارسول الله

rows.speaker: الحسن وعائشة
rows.claim: Al-Durr al-Manthur also transmits reports from al-Hasan and Aisha about the Prophet reciting lines of poetry.
rows.anchor: وروى في الدر المنثور الخبرين عن الحسن وعائشة كما رواه

rows.speaker: مجمع البيان
rows.claim: On 'I am the prophet, no lie; I am the son of Abd al-Muttalib,' some say it is not poetry, while others call its meter accidental and unintentional; al-Tabataba'i says rejecting the report is easier than denying the line is poetry or deliberate verse.
rows.anchor: فأما قوله أنا النبي لا كذب أنا ابن عبد المطلب فقد قال قوم إن هذا ليس بشعر

rows.speaker: علي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report attributed to Ali interprets 'whoever is alive' as whoever is rational.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المراد بمن كان حيا عاقلا وروي ذلك عن علي عليه السلام

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Qummi reports from Abu al-Jarud, from al-Baqir, that the idols cannot help their worshippers, who instead stand as a present host for the idols.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي في رواية أبي الجارود عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام

rows.speaker: أبي بن خلف
rows.claim: Al-Ayyashi transmits from al-Sadiq that Ubayy ibn Khalaf crumbled a decayed bone and challenged the resurrection; God answered that the one who first created it will revive it.
rows.anchor: عن الحلبي عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال جاء أبي بن خلف فأخذ عظما باليا من حائط ففته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعروة بن الزبير وقتادة والسدي وعكرمة
rows.claim: Al-Durr al-Manthur gives many routes for a similar report, while other reports from Ibn Abbas name al-As ibn Wa'il or Abd Allah ibn Ubayy as the challenger.
rows.anchor: وروى مثله في الدر المنثور بطرق كثيرة عن ابن عباس وعروة بن الزبير وعن قتادة والسدي وعكرمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i notes the alternate attributions of the bone challenge to al-As ibn Wa'il and Abd Allah ibn Ubayy in other Ibn Abbas reports.
rows.anchor: وروى أيضا عن ابن عباس أن القائل هو العاص بن وائل وبطريق آخر عنه أن القائل هو عبد الله بن أبي

rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: In al-Ihtijaj, al-Sadiq answers that the soul remains after leaving the body until the trumpet is blown; then created things perish and are recreated as they began, after a four-hundred-year interval between the two blasts.
rows.anchor: وفي الاحتجاج في احتجاج أبي عبد الله الصادق عليه السلام قال السائل أفيتلاشى الروح بعد خروجه عن قالبه أم هو باق
